data.gender_notes: Ebraheem is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ebraheem is the Arabic variant of Abraham, meaning 'father of many'. It signifies a leader and a figure of great importance in Islamic tradition. The name Ebraheem carries the meaning “Father of many” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ebraheem usually hope their child will grow to embody father of many and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In the Quran, Prophet Ebraheem is considered a prominent figure and a role model for his unwavering faith and trust in Allah.
data.etymology: Ebraheem belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Father of many.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ebraheem total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Ebraheem's name holds significant cultural importance in Islamic tradition. Prophet Abraham is considered one of the most important figures in Islamic history and is revered for his unwavering faith and obedience to God. His story and teachings have been passed down through generations, shaping the cultural and religious views in the Islamic world. Ebraheem is also mentioned frequently in the Quran and Hadiths, further emphasizing his importance.
data.spiritual_significance: Ebraheem's name carries a deep spiritual significance. His story teaches us about the importance of faith, submission to God, and obedience to His commands. Abraham's willingness to sacrifice his son Ishmael at God's command demonstrates his unwavering faith and willingness to put God above all else. Ebraheem's faith and trust in God's plan serves as an inspiration for Muslims to trust in Allah's plan and remain steadfast in their faith. Additionally, his name Ebraheem, which means 'father of many', signifies the idea of bringing new believers into the fold and expanding the faith through procreation and spreading knowledge.
